summary: The EASI score calculator takes the numbers you enter and reports head and neck score adult immediately. It is free to use, needs no account, and shows the working rather than just the answer. That makes it useful for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. Nothing is submitted anywhere: the arithmetic runs in the page you are looking at.

sections.title: How does the EASI score calculator work?
sections.html:
The EASI score calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports head and neck score adult in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the redness (Head and neck), the thickness (Head and neck) and the scratching (Head and neck)); then you type in the EASI score, the lower limbs score adult, the upper limbs score adult and the severity score head and neck adult.

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the EASI score calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Head and neck score adult=EASI score − lower limbs score adult − trunk score adult − upper limbs score adult
Area score=((how old is the patient? < 2) ? ( head and neck score adult ÷ (severity score head and neck adult × (1 ÷ 10)) ) : ( head and neck score adult ÷ (severity score head and neck adult × (1 ÷ 5)) ))
Trunk score adult=(3 ÷ 10) × area score × severity score trunk adult
Area score=5 × upper limbs score adult ÷ severity score upper limbs adult
Severity score lower limbs adult=((how old is the patient? < 2) ? ( lower limbs score adult ÷ (area score × (2 ÷ 5)) ) : ( lower limbs score adult ÷ (area score × (3 ÷ 10)) ))
Lichenification=-redness − scratching + severity score head and neck adult − thickness

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The EASI score calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.

faq.q: What does the EASI score calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns head and neck score adult. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the EASI score calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for a few values, which is 21 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (21 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports EASI score = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the EASI score calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
